title: A Sigil for the Spire
premise: Rosalind Winterbourne survives in the magic-dead valley by stealing memories from travelers and selling them back to the lonely. When a dying stranger presses a map into her hands, she learns it leads to the Spire of Vael, where a sigil sleeps that could reignite the ancient war between mages and mortals—and the stranger's memories, which Rosalind accidentally absorbed, mark her as the sigil's heir. Hunted by the Order of the Thirteenth Moon, Rosalind flees the valley with a disgraced archivist and a runaway mage-child who slowly become the family she never had. At the Spire, she must choose between destroying the sigil and claiming its power; she shatters it, scattering her stolen memories—including her own forgotten childhood—to the people she loves, and finally belongs somewhere by choice rather than blood.
about_author: Mara Marchetti is a former archivist who left academia to write fantasy about outsiders forging their own legacies. She lives near a valley she insists is fictional, where she collects maps and refuses to explain why.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Things
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In the memory-market of Hollowvale, Rosalind steals a dying stranger's final memories along with his coin purse, and finds inside them a burning map and a name that isn't hers: heir of Vael. As Order hunters arrive asking questions, she realizes the valley's magic-dead borders won't hide her forever. Emotional beat: terror of being seen after a lifetime of invisibility.

chapters.title: Three Against the Thirteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, with interludes from the child Wren. Fleeing through the mountain passes, Rosalind grudgingly gathers companions: Cassian, an archivist exiled for knowing too much, and Wren, a mage-child the Order wants erased. The stranger's absorbed memories begin bleeding into Rosalind's dreams, teaching her the sigil's location and its terrible cost. Emotional beat: reluctant trust hardening into something like family.

chapters.title: What the Spire Remembers
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV as they reach the Spire of Vael on the eve of the thirteenth turn. The Order ambushes them at the gates; Wren is taken, and Cassian learns Rosalind has been hiding that claiming the sigil would erase every memory she's ever stolen—including the ones that made her love him and Wren. Emotional beat: betrayal, sacrifice, and the choice between power and people.

chapters.title: A Sigil Broken, A Name Kept
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Inside the Spire, Rosalind confronts the Order's leader—who reveals she was once a stolen child of Vael herself—and chooses to shatter the sigil rather than claim it, releasing her hoarded memories to everyone she's touched. Wren is freed; the war dies unborn. In the quiet after, Rosalind keeps only one memory as her own: the moment they became a family. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.
